problem: LVLM-based VLN agents suffer perception (visual hallucination), reasoning (left/right confusion) and planning errors. Existing visual prompts are fragmented and rarely exploit multi-view input, and process-based RFT such as GiGPO needs identical anchor states, which is costly in continuous navigation.
motivation: LVLMs are weak at depth and spatial understanding, and long-horizon navigation gives only sparse outcome rewards. The authors observe that a state-independent step reward lets steps from any state be compared. This makes flexible step grouping possible without anchor states.
key_idea: Combine a dual-view (front view + BEV) visual prompt that turns navigation into VQA with SRGPO, an RFT algorithm that computes step-level advantages over randomly grouped steps using a state-independent verifiable process reward.
insight: The VP ablation shows dual view alone hurts (GPT-4.1 0.450 vs 0.650 for FV only), and only the full combination of bounding box, action projection, agent marker, navigation line and view alignment gives 0.867. So the modules work jointly. For RFT, a state-independent process reward removes the need for identical-state grouping. Larger step groups then cost no extra rollouts (N_S=8 gives 0.411 vs 0.723 at N_S=16). GiGPO with the same VPR reaches similar training success but converges slower and generalizes worse (0.572).
method: Dual-view input: front view (FV) and bird's-eye view (BEV) are concatenated into one image and fed to the LVLM.
Bounding box + navigation line: the target is boxed in both views, and a navigation arrow runs from the agent to the target (from the bottom-middle of the FV, from the agent centre in the BEV).

Agent marker + view alignment: a circle with a yellow left side, purple right side and a green heading arrow marks the agent in the BEV, and the BEV is rotated so the agent always faces forward, matching the FV.
Action projection: movement actions are drawn as numbered arrows in the BEV and rotation actions in the FV, so planning becomes choosing an arrow (VQA).
Verifiable process reward (VPR): step reward is 1 if the distance to the target decreases, or else if the target newly enters the FV, otherwise 0. An invalid action is penalized with lambda=0.1.

SRGPO: episode-level GRPO advantage A_E plus omega(0.5) times a step-level advantage A_S. A_S is normalized within groups of N_S=16 steps sampled randomly from the whole batch, and the advantage is used in a PPO-clip objective with a KL term.
Training setup: Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct with VP embedded throughout, rollout group size 4, max 20 steps, trained on i.d. (60 randomized base scenes) or o.o.d. (60 new AI2-THOR scenes) scenes.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct (RFT with SRGPO) and GPT-4.1 (frozen, zero-shot with VP)
setting.training_data: RFT on randomized AI2-THOR scenes (60 base scenes i.d. or 60 new o.o.d. scenes), 150 epochs i.d. / 100 epochs o.o.d.; SFT baseline uses GPT-4.1 expert trajectories on i.d. scenes; GPT-4.1+VP is training-free
setting.observation: concatenated BEV + first-person RGB image with visual prompts, plus text action history (window 5) and env feedback
setting.action_space: 8 discrete low-level actions: move forward/backward/right/left 0.25 m, rotate right/left, tilt up/down
setting.privileged: Target object location and position are used to draw the bounding box and navigation line in the VP, and GT distance and visibility are used for the training reward

numbers.extra: RFT on i.d. scenes, last-epoch model, mean±std over 3 runs; uses GT target info for VP
training-free; uses GT target info for VP
ablation baseline trained with the proposed VPR reward

numbers_note: Only success rate is reported. Training curves and the N_S=8 result (mean SR 0.411, std 0.103) are given in text or figures.
results: GPT-4.1+VP reaches 86.7% SR on EmbodiedBench Navigation, versus 65.0% for vanilla GPT-4.1 and 66.7% for the best closed model, Claude-3.5-Sonnet. VP+SRGPO on Qwen2.5-VL-3B reaches 72.3%, beating InternVL3-78B (66.7%), VP+GiGPO with VPR (57.2%), VP+GRPO (40.8%) and VP+SFT (36.7%).
limitations: Evaluated only on one small benchmark (60 in-room AI2-THOR tasks); the authors plan to test on more diverse and complex benchmarks.
VP relies on GT target location and object visibility, and the authors note that perception modules to generate VP are future work.
SRGPO relies on a state-independent process reward, which is only well-defined for certain tasks.
